transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Moreno (Redwood Sec), Maya Rinaldi (LyricAI Head of Security), Jonas Hsu (LyricAI CTO), Priya Menon (Legal), Ethan Park (Platform)

Summary:
LyricAI is evaluating Redwood for embedding and chat inferencing for EU and US customers; primary concerns are strict data residency, region pinning per-tenant, clear subprocessor inventory for EU audit, and KMS/HSM options for key custody. They also want to understand cross-border fallback behavior and what telemetry/logs leave the region. Discussed SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/RBAC integration, and an engineering benchmark for EU latency. Next steps captured.

Topics discussed:
- Data residency and per-tenant region pinning
- Cross-border processing and fallback policies
- Sub-processor list and EU subcontractor details
- KMS integrations, HSM, and key escrow options
- Audit logs, retention, and access controls
- SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC mapping for LyricAI org

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Avery: ok thanks everyone for joining uh we wanted to run through LyricAI's requirements around region pinning and the subprocessor matrix. i'll hand to Samir to do a quick tech overview then leah will cover security attestation stuff.
[00:00:22] Samir: thanks avery hi all, i'll start with the high level. Redwood supports per-tenant region affinity. you can pin a workspace to EU-west-1 or us-west-2, and requests will ideally stay in that region. We do have automatic fallbacks if capacity is exhausted. i'll explain routing policies in a bit.
[00:00:40] Maya: quick clarifying question — when you say "stay in that region" does that include logs and telemetry? we need to ensure no plaintext payload or logs egress to the us for EU customers.
[00:00:55] Leah: good question maya. by default request payloads and KV caches are kept in region for pinned workspaces. logs that are required for platform health are aggregated to the control plane — that control plane can be run as private (for Redwood Private) but for hosted customers we provide a regional control plane option. we do send anonymized usage metrics out of region unless you opt into our private plane.
[00:01:15] Jonas: how does that look from a subprocesser standpoint — who in your stack would potentially touch eu data? we need a clear subprocessor list for our privacy team.
[00:01:30] Avery: we have a published subprocessor list; i'll share the latest spreadsheet after this call. important ones for EU are our cloud provider (GCP in europe), monitoring vendor, and model hosting partners for older model variants. For Private deployments you get more control — fewer subprocessors.
[00:01:50] Priya: is that subprocessor list SOC 2 scoped? we need to confirm whether subprocessors are included in the scope of your attestation.
[00:02:05] Leah: yes our SOC 2 covers key subprocessors, the attestation pdf lists scope and the date. i'll attach the SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certs. note sometimes model vendors are micro-subprocessors and listed separately — we can provide a flatten list for EU audit.
[00:02:22] Ethan: on KMS, can we bring our own key? we want client-side keys in KMS to ensure plaintext never stored outside our control.
[00:02:36] Samir: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) via integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and some HSM partners. Redwood can be configured so the model server envelopes with your key — we have a KMS plugin. for Private installs you can do a local HSM. there is also an optional escrow path for long-term recovery.
[00:02:58] Maya: if we use BYOK, what's the live rotation procedure? and is there any key material that ever moves to Redwood's control plane?
[00:03:12] Leah: good questions. key rotation is orchestrated by your KMS; Redwood uses the public key to encrypt at rest metadata and does not store plaintext keys. for certain managed-ops flows we require limited service account tokens, but we can put those behind customer-managed CMKs so even service tokens cannot decrypt without a KMS op. i'll follow up with the exact KMS flow diagram.
[00:03:35] Jonas: about fallback behavior — say EU region gets saturated, do you route to US? what are our options to avoid cross-border processing?
[00:03:48] Samir: by default our smart router prefers the pinned region and will only failover to a compatible model in another region if you enable cross-region fallback. there are three policies: strict (reject if capacity not available), regional-fallback (queue or delayed), and global-fallback (route to other region). for LyricAI given compliance needs we recommend strict or regional-fallback with a short queue and an alert if capacity is low.
[00:04:12] Maya: strict sounds safer. if we choose strict, how will we handle spikes — do you provide burst capacity?
[00:04:24] Avery: yes we have reserved capacity and burst credits; reserved pools can be committed per month. for EU we can provision dedicated nodes. pricing and lead times vary — i'll send the options.
[00:04:38] Priya: we also need to understand audit logs — who can access them and for how long are request/response logs retained?
[00:04:48] Leah: request-level payload retention is configurable; default retention for hosted is 30 days for full logs and 365 for metadata. for EU regulated data we can enable shorter retention or redact PII from logs. Access is role-gated via RBAC and SSO; logs are accessible only to RBAC roles you map via SAML/SCIM.
[00:05:04] Ethan: i want to confirm that log search does not send raw prompts to an external SaaS. which vendor holds the log index?
[00:05:15] Leah: our log indexing is done by a managed vendor in-region for EU tenants — we can also bring a vendor-of-choice via Private. if you need, we can do customer-managed log storage.
[00:05:30] Maya: about subprocessors — are model weights ever served from a us-based partner for EU-pinned requests? we've seen vendors cache models cross-border.
[00:05:42] Samir: good point. model snapshot hosting is the tricky bit. we replicate model shards to the region for pinned workloads; however, some third-party model repos we use replicate globally. we can provide a list and mark which models have EU-local hosting. if a particular open model is only available via a global repo we can vendor-constrain or use an alternate model.
[00:06:05] Jonas: can we enforce model-variants to be EU-only? for example force quantized variants hosted in eu to avoid cross-border inference.
[00:06:16] Samir: yes you can pin model variants per workspace. the catalogue has an EU-local flag and we can gate rollout to EU-hosted variants.
[00:06:25] Priya: will you provide a signed addendum to the DPA that enumerates subprocessors and region commitments?
[00:06:34] Avery: yes we can do an addendum. standard DPA has a subprocessors section; if you need specific contractual language on geo-binding we can provide a data residency addendum for enterprise deals.
[00:06:44] Maya: one more — what about personnel access, like runbook access from engineering in other regions? we need to know if ops engineers outside EU can access customer data during incident response.
[00:06:58] Leah: access is audited via SSO and RBAC; for EU-pinned tenants we can limit operator roles to EU-based admins and require just-in-time access with approval and ticketing. all privileged ops are logged to audit trail.
[00:07:15] Ethan: does Redwood expose a live audit log stream for our SIEM? we'd like to push logs to our Splunk in Dublin.
[00:07:26] Samir: yes you can forward audit logs to your Splunk/ELK via secure forwarder and keep them in-region. we support syslog over TLS and S3 buckets for archival.
[00:07:36] Maya: ok what about encryption in transit — do you terminate TLS at your edge? sometimes load balancers in front of endpoints are outside region.
[00:07:49] Leah: TLS is terminated at regional ingress points for pinned workspaces. for private installs you can bring your own LB. we also support mTLS between internal services if you want additional crypto.
[00:08:02] Priya: will you share SOC 2 and ISO evidence? and can we get a scope statement that shows EU subprocessors included?
[00:08:12] Leah: i'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs and a scope extract. i'll also include the subprocessor manifest flattened for EU.
[00:08:22] Jonas: i want to plan a bench: can Samir run a quick throughput and p99 latency test from eu-west-1 with our sample prompt set, ideally with pinned workspace? we want numbers before procurement decision.
[00:08:34] Samir: yes we can spin up a pinned workspace and run a small benchmark. i suggest we run three variants: hosted EU default, hosted EU with strict policy, and dedicated reserved nodes. that'll give you delta on cost vs latency.
[00:08:50] Maya: do you have a playbook for incident response when data potentially leaves region accidentally? we need communications timelines, forensic steps, and contact points.
[00:09:03] Avery: yes we have an incident response playbook and SLA commitments for breaches; i'll include the IR playbook and escalation contacts.
[00:09:12] Priya: legal wants confirmation about indemnities related to subprocessors in the EU. can we get the legal team to review and confirm?
[00:09:22] Avery: noted — i'll loop in our legal ops.
[00:09:28] Maya: any known limitations on SSO — we use Okta and will need SCIM group sync.
[00:09:36] Leah: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for group provisioning. mapping uses roles that you define in Redwood. sometimes attribute mappings need a quick mapping sheet; we'll share an example.
[00:09:50] Ethan: a small nit: we heard from another vendor that they retained plaintext user prompts in error logs. can you confirm redwood's default is to not keep request bodies longer than retention window and to optionally redact?
[00:10:04] Leah: default does not store them beyond retention windows; we also offer prompt redaction and PII scrubbing plugin which you can enable for EU tenants.
[00:10:15] Jonas: great. are there any blockers from Redwood's side to sign a data residency addendum?
[00:10:23] Avery: no blockers, just commercial terms on reserved capacity and standard DPA modifications.
[00:10:29] Maya: ok let's finish with next steps and owners.

[00:10:35] Recap / Next steps:
- Avery to send: latest subprocessor spreadsheet, pricing options for reserved EU capacity, DPA/data residency addendum draft, IR playbook (owner: Avery)
- Samir to run: EU pinned workspace benchmark and share latency/cost spreadsheet (owner: Samir)
- Leah to attach: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, KMS integration diagram, and list of EU-local model variants (owner: Leah)
- LyricAI (Maya/Priya) to send: specific compliance rider language and priority model list for EU-local hosting (owner: Maya/Priya)

[00:11:05] Closing notes:
Maya: thanks all. we'll review the DPA addendum and get legal back to you by the 12/8 benchmark week.
Avery: thanks, we'll get the attachments out today and follow up on scheduling the benchmark.
[00:11:25] End of recording

Notes on transcription quality: medium. Occasional mis-attributions and some technical names transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "K V cache" instead of "KV cache", "Sample" for SAML).
